title.text:
Europe carries 3.7 times the Gulf's freight per passenger, and distance does not explain it
Corridors ordered by sector length, shortest at the top. The correlation between the two is -0.10, so belly freight tracks what two economies trade rather than how far apart they are: East Asia is the densest at 130 kg on only 2.0M passengers, while North America is the longest corridor and near the bottom. Physical units, no revenue assumption. DGCA counts freight on the same first-foreign-point sector as passengers, so connecting tonnage flatters the Gulf here exactly as it does elsewhere

annotations.text: Source: Freight and passengers from DGCA international country statistics via github.com/Vonter/india-aviation-traffic (ODbL); corridor reference distances are great circle from OurAirports (CC0). Physical units only, no revenue assumption
